exposure_at_1000_steps.C0: ~1,908 of 64,000 draws are 1-1 = 0.82 epochs over the full index

test: exact paired sign-flip permutation over seeds; floor 2/2^10 = 0.00195
verdict: **No. Training on 1-1 alone does not beat the full corpus, and the peak does not move later.** Early walls are flat-to-slightly-up and null (goomba/pipe1/pipe2 C1 +2.5 pp, 7/10 seeds, p=0.242; pipe3 +1.8 pp, 7/10, p=0.469). **Late walls go DOWN in both arms with the same sign and the same seed count: pipe 4 C1 -3.2 pp (1/10 seeds up, p=0.035), C2 -4.0 pp (1/10 up, p=0.022); frontier C1 -1.6 pp (1/10, p=0.023).** On-top failures at pipe 4 rise (C1 +3.8, p=0.053; C2 +3.5, p=0.033). **Nothing survives Bonferroni over the 14 wall tests** and none of it was pre-specified, so no single p-value is claimed. What is claimed is the replication: two independently trained arms, opposite corpus mixtures, same sign at the same walls, 1 of 10 seeds up in each - corroborated by the ladder, where the collapse is monotone and arrives ~9x earlier in steps than the full corpus's. **Third branch: the off-task levels were acting as regularisation, and 2,323 samples cannot support this model.** Completions are null in both directions (C0 0.4, C1 0.7, C2 0.7 per 200 per seed; p=0.625) on counts far too small to carry weight. Floor 2/2^10 = 0.00195, stated with every p above.
pipe1_pipe2_identity_note: pipe1 (470) and pipe2 (630) clearance are identical in every arm and in the scripted control too: no episode in this project has ever failed between pipe 1's far edge and pipe 2's. The two thresholds are not independent measurements.
